correctness.rationale: For every integrable rate in [0,R], the Poisson parity identity produces an exact exponential-kernel energy for its cumulative-hazard pushforward. Lipschitz rate cap implies mu>=dx/(RT) on [0,B]. At c>1/(1+B) the stated candidate has a potential minimized exactly at the two endpoints; positive signed-measure kernel energy makes the variational inequality strict away from the candidate. At smaller c the classical constant-potential equilibrium is feasible. The pulse realizes either minimizer and the endpoint cost is computed by exact integration; a Fourier-transform proof supplies strict positive definiteness for any finite signed measure. Independent ODE matrix-exponential checks passed 90 parameter instances and 250 admissible randomly sampled protocols. Numerical checks supplement, but do not substitute for, the analytic global proof.

originality.rationale: The 2012 Alfonsi–Schied exponential-kernel equilibrium measure exactly covers the UNCONSTRAINED subproblem, and this is credited. The new question adds the physically imposed pointwise switching-rate cap, which induces a lower density obstacle in hazard space. The explicit constrained equilibrium and sharp saturated-to-unsaturated phase boundary are proved with a separate variational inequality, not asserted to follow verbatim from the 2012 unconstrained theorem. The 2026 primary model studies distinct endpoint steering/minimum work, and the closest published periodic-reversal allocation theorem optimizes a different long-time quantity. A potentially equivalent unindexed bounded-impact execution theorem remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: The old unbounded-cap equilibrium measure is known, not new; any originality rests specifically on the rate cap and its exact penalty.
Older constrained exponential-kernel execution or optimal-control literature might contain an equivalent density-floor variational inequality not returned in targeted searches.
The theorem does not extend to harmonic confinement; adding a nonconstant response weight changes the feasible measure obstacle.

value.rationale: A sharp cap is operationally natural for molecular-motor reversal controls: a prescribed expected number of flips must be allocated within a finite observation period. The unique centered pulse, sharp threshold R=(1+B)/T, and exact positive quadratic performance loss in the hardware-limited regime give structural design information not available from ordinary constant-tumbling rates or the known unrestricted capacitary formula. The result solves all parameters B,T,R,v in its natural finite-horizon model, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
